terms.grammar: vocative of dominus, used in address
evidence: Sen. Ep. 3.1 (Lewis & Short: “in respectful greeting, like our Sir”)
terms.comment: By Seneca’s day one greeted a man whose name escaped one as dominus (Sen. Ep. 3.1, cited by Morgan–Owens s.v. Mr.); earlier it is what a slave called his master. To a woman, domina.

terms.grammar: vocative of domina, used in address

terms.comment: Friendly or ironic, mostly in comedy (Lewis & Short s.v. bonus); Traupman gives it for “sir!” to an equal.

phrases.latin: Cupiō, domine, sī id pāce liceat tuā.
phrases.english: I should like to, sir, if you will allow it.

phrases.latin: age tū, illūc prōcēde, bone vir!
phrases.english: come on, you, step forward, my good man!
